subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree was a cleric of Lolth who had also become, in some capacity, a cleric of Zuggtmoy, and in the end she had been indistinguishable from the rot she served.
source_quote: Asha Vandree had been a cleric of Lolth who had also become, in some capacity, a cleric of Zuggtmoy, and in the end she had been indistinguishable from the rot she served.

subject: holy symbol of Lolth
fact: Asha Vandree possessed a holy symbol of Lolth.
source_quote: The holy symbol of Lolth.

subject: chain mail
fact: Asha Vandree wore chain mail.
source_quote: Chain mail.

subject: prayer beads
fact: Asha Vandree carried prayer beads.
source_quote: Prayer beads.

subject: sealed wax pouch
fact: Asha Vandree carried a sealed wax pouch.
source_quote: And a sealed wax pouch.

subject: Drow cloak
fact: Asha Vandree wore a Drow cloak of fine spider-silk that drinks shadow.
source_quote: Zalthir took the Drow cloak she'd been wearing — the fine spider-silk kind that drinks shadow.

subject: wax pouch contents
fact: The sealed wax pouch contained pages of close, careful script — the handwriting of someone who had once been methodical, who had trained as a theologian and brought that training to bear on a question that should not have been asked.
source_quote: Inside were pages of close, careful script — the handwriting of someone who had once been methodical, who had trained as a theologian and brought that training to bear on a question that should not have been asked.

subject: theological text
fact: The wax pouch contained a theological exploration claiming that Zuggtmoy and Lolth are the same thing.
source_quote: It's basically a long theological exploration of why Zuggtmoy and Lolth — and claiming that Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same thing.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara was a high priestess of Lolth who had been actively subverted by Zuggtmoy.
source_quote: Ilvara was a high priestess of Lolth who had been actively subverted by Zuggtmoy.

subject: Ilvara's prayer book
fact: Ilvara's prayer book was a standard Lolth devotional text with marginalia in a different hand, documenting her corruption timeline.
source_quote: The main text was a standard Lolth prayer book — the kind of thing they give to promising young acolytes in the outer sanctums of any major drow religious house. The marginalia told the story. A different hand. That detail mattered to me more than any of the specific words.

subject: Ilvara's marginalia
fact: The marginalia in Ilvara's prayer book showed a gradual shift from formal prayer to associative, unstructured writing, indicating psychological corruption.
source_quote: Then, gradually, around the margins, a second voice crept in. Less structured. More associative. The sentences didn't always end. Some of them were questions that answered themselves with other questions.

subject: sealed orders from House Mizzrym
fact: The sealed orders from House Mizzrym were frantic inquiries demanding Ilvara's location and activities after her disappearance.
source_quote: Where are you? What have you been doing? Respond — kind of thing. You've gone missing. Followed by more frantic: where are you, where are you? Didn't you read the previous memo? What's up?

subject: letter from Neverlight Grove
fact: The letter from Neverlight Grove recorded a missed political meeting, indicating Ilvara’s allegiance had shifted beyond diplomatic reach.
source_quote: A missed meeting. Political correspondence that had gone nowhere, because the person it was addressed to had gone somewhere else — somewhere a Demon Queen's influence had been a stronger pull than any political alliance.

subject: Living Serpent Head Scourge
fact: The Living Serpent Head Scourge was a scourge whose head was an actual living serpent, or had been, in some intermediate state between alive and not.
source_quote: The Living Serpent Head Scourge sounds... it sounds like a great museum piece. A scourge whose head was an actual living serpent, or had been, in some intermediate state between alive and not.

subject: water-damaged prisoner journal
fact: A water-damaged journal from a prisoner who had written things down and then presumably stopped being able to, with swollen pages, run ink, and visible handwriting in drier sections.
source_quote: We also found a water-damaged journal from a prisoner we would never meet — someone who had written things down and then, presumably, stopped being able to. I held it carefully. The pages were swollen and the ink had run in places, but the handwriting was still visible in the drier sections, the marks of a person who had kept records right up until they couldn't.

subject: flask of Overbright brandy
fact: A flask of Overbright brandy was received with considerable personal interest.
source_quote: The flask of Overbright brandy I received with considerably more personal interest.

subject: confiscated prisoner belongings
fact: Confiscated prisoner belongings included Thorin’s tooth, which Ilvara had carried as a trophy.
source_quote: Confiscated prisoner belongings. Ilvara had been carrying it. Of course she had — she was exactly the sort of high priestess who would keep trophies, who would drag along evidence of her ownership of people... I opened it, and the contents were exactly what you would expect... 'like your tooth, Thorin.'... He reached in and found it. He held it for a moment without saying anything.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin’s tooth had been taken and carried by Ilvara as a trophy of ownership.
source_quote: 'like your tooth, Thorin.'... Oh, yeah. I want my tooth back.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir took the Drow cloak from Asha Vandree’s body.
source_quote: Zalthir took the Drow cloak she'd been wearing — the fine spider-silk kind that drinks shadow.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was cataloguing the room and paying close attention to implications of recovered items.
source_quote: Daz looked over from where he was already cataloguing the rest of the room. Daz was paying attention in the way he pays attention to things — still, cataloguing, already working the implications.

subject: Gorg'Bahamut
fact: Gorg'Bahamut was the narrator's mentor, who would have wanted a pious ritual performed over the dead.
source_quote: My mentor Gorg'Bahamut would have wanted me to.

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud sat down across from Protanther after four hundred years of preparation and still had a blind spot.
source_quote: I thought, briefly, of Stroud sitting down across from Protanther. Four hundred years of preparation. Still had a blind spot.

subject: Protanther
fact: Protanther was the subject of Stroud’s long preparation and eventual blind spot.
source_quote: I thought, briefly, of Stroud sitting down across from Protanther. Four hundred years of preparation. Still had a blind spot.

subject: Tongued merchant
fact: A merchant once known to the narrator had been Tongued by a bardic curse, producing correspondence eerily similar to Ilvara’s marginalia.
source_quote: I had seen something like this before, in a completely different context — a merchant I once knew who had been Tongued by a bardic curse, whose correspondence from that period was eerily similar.

subject: Underdark
fact: Ilvara had been carrying Thorin’s tooth around the Underdark.
source_quote: she had been carrying his tooth around the Underdark.

subject: prayer book marginalia
fact: The marginalia in Ilvara’s prayer book showed a corruption timeline, beginning with formal prayer and evolving into associative, unstructured writing indicating psychological fragmentation.
source_quote: The early entries were neat and formal and exactly what you would expect. Then, gradually, around the margins, a second voice crept in. Less structured. More associative. The sentences didn't always end. Some of them were questions that answered themselves with other questions.

subject: wax pouch contents
fact: The wax pouch contained a theological text arguing that Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same entity, demonstrating theological contortion from a desired conclusion backward.
source_quote: It was very well-argued. It was also completely mad. It was the written record of a mind finding its way toward the conclusion that two incompatible things were secretly one thing — the kind of reasoning that starts from a desired destination and works backward.

subject: sealed orders from House Mizzrym
fact: The sealed orders from House Mizzrym were official inquiries into Ilvara’s disappearance, escalating from formal to frantic.
source_quote: Where are you? What have you been doing? Respond — kind of thing. You've gone missing. Followed by more frantic: where are you, where are you? Didn't you read the previous memo? What's up?

subject: letter from Neverlight Grove
fact: The letter from Neverlight Grove was a record of a missed political meeting, indicating Ilvara’s allegiance had shifted beyond diplomatic reach.
source_quote: A missed meeting. Political correspondence that had gone nowhere, because the person it was addressed to had gone somewhere else — somewhere a Demon Queen's influence had been a stronger pull than any political alliance.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym had been attempting to locate Ilvara and had not yet learned of her corruption or death.
source_quote: House Mizzrym would learn eventually, I supposed. We had helped with that.

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove had expected to meet Ilvara, but the meeting was missed due to her corruption and disappearance.
source_quote: A missed meeting. Political correspondence that had gone nowhere, because the person it was addressed to had gone somewhere else — somewhere a Demon Queen's influence had been a stronger pull than any political alliance.

subject: Living Serpent Head Scourge
fact: The Living Serpent Head Scourge was a weapon of remarkable craftsmanship and terrible origin, intended for display as a museum piece.
source_quote: It sounds like a great museum piece. There is a tradition, in certain temples I have visited, of displaying items that are terrible in origin and remarkable in craft, on the theory that acknowledging the craft is not the same as endorsing what the craft served.

subject: water-damaged prisoner journal
fact: The water-damaged prisoner journal contained visible handwriting in drier sections, indicating the prisoner had kept records up until they could no longer.
source_quote: The handwriting was still visible in the drier sections, the marks of a person who had kept records right up until they couldn't.

source_quote: The flask of Overbright brandy I received with considerably more personal interest.

source_quote: Confiscated prisoner belongings. Ilvara had been carrying it. Of course she had — she was exactly the sort of high priestess who would keep trophies, who would drag along evidence of her ownership of people...
